title: Amending the Osero Artifact runs a four-stage Root Edit: holder proposal, Facilitator alignment review, token vote, then Facilitator-executed edit
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.1 defines Osero's Routine Protocol for the Root Edit Primitive — the process by which the Agent's own Artifact is amended in non-emergency conditions. Four stages run in fixed order.

1. **Submission** (.1.1): "The Root Edit process begins with an OSERO token holder submitting a proposal through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal." The holder "must hold at least 1% of the circulating token supply," and the proposal must also be posted on the Sky Forum under the "Osero Prime" category.
2. **Facilitator review** (.1.3): within seven days the Operational Facilitator must review the proposal for alignment and announce the finding on the Forum post.
3. **Token holder vote** (.1.4): only "where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment" does the Facilitator trigger a Snapshot poll — open three days, requiring 10% of circulating supply participating and 50% in favor.
4. **Execution** (.1.5): on approval the Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse; "regardless of the outcome," they record the vote result and pertinent documents.

The structure is a dual-key: token holders supply legitimacy, the Facilitator supplies alignment screening and execution. Neither can amend the Artifact alone — holders cannot reach a vote without a favourable review, and the Facilitator cannot edit without a passing poll.

The timeline is also deliberately short for a constitutional process: seven days of review plus three days of voting means an Artifact amendment can complete in under two weeks, trading deliberation time for responsiveness.
description: Only holders of at least 1% of circulating OSERO can propose; a 3-day Snapshot poll needs 10% participation and a simple majority; the Facilitator executes the approved edit.
